title: Indefinite Pronouns
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Has dominado el uso de los pronombres indefinidos.

parts.visual: SOME (Afirmativas): Someone / Somebody (Alguien), Something (Algo), Somewhere (En algún lugar). Ej: Someone called you (Alguien te llamó).
parts.audio: SOME is used in affirmative sentences. Someone or somebody means 'alguien'. Something means 'algo'. Somewhere means 'en algún lugar'. Example: Someone called you.

parts.visual: ANY (Preguntas y Negativas): Anyone / Anybody (Alguien/Nadie), Anything (Algo/Nada), Anywhere (En algún/ningún lugar). Ej: Is anyone here? (¿Hay alguien aquí?). I don't know anything (No sé nada).
parts.audio: ANY is used in questions and negative sentences. Anyone or anybody. Anything. Anywhere. Examples: Is anyone here? I don't know anything.

parts.visual: NO (Negativas sin 'not'): No one / Nobody (Nadie), Nothing (Nada), Nowhere (En ningún lugar). Ej: Nobody knows (Nadie sabe). I have nothing to say (No tengo nada que decir). EVERY (Todos): Everyone, Everything, Everywhere.
parts.audio: NO is used for negative meanings, but the verb must be affirmative. No one or nobody means 'nadie'. Nothing means 'nada'. Nowhere means 'en ningún lugar'. Examples: Nobody knows. I have nothing to say. Finally, EVERY means all. Everyone, Everything, Everywhere.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el pronombre indefinido correcto para cada situación en la oficina.

questions.question: I need to tell you ____ important. (Algo - Afirmativa).
Does ____ have a pen I can borrow? (¿Alguien? - Pregunta).
I'm sorry, there is ____ I can do. (Nada - verbo en afirmativo).
questions.explanation: 'There is nothing' = No hay nada. (Doble negación es incorrecta en inglés).

questions.question: I don't know ____ about the new project. (Nada - verbo en negativo).
questions.explanation: Con el verbo negativo 'don't know', usamos 'anything'.

questions.question: ____ is ready for the presentation. We can start. (Todo).
____ left their laptop on the desk. (Alguien - Afirmativa).
We looked ____ for the missing document. (En todos lados).
I can't find my keys ____. (En ningún lugar - verbo negativo).
____ wants to work on Sunday. (Nadie - verbo afirmativo).
Did you see ____ in the meeting room? (¿A alguien? - Pregunta).
I have ____ to go for lunch. Let's eat here. (Ningún lugar).
questions.explanation: Verbo afirmativo (have) + nowhere = No tengo ningún lugar.

questions.question: Hello? Is ____ there? (¿Hay alguien ahí?).
____ agreed with the CEO's decision. (Todos).
Let's go ____ quiet to talk. (A algún lugar - Afirmativa).
There is ____ wrong with the server. It's offline. (Algo).
I knocked on the door, but ____ answered. (Nadie).
questions.explanation: No one = nadie (tambié se puede usar nobody).

questions.question: Do you need ____ from the store? (¿Algo? - Pregunta).
The office is empty. ____ has gone home. (Todos).
There isn't ____ milk in the fridge. (Nada - verbo negativo).
questions.explanation: Con sustantivos incontables, 'any' significa 'nada de' en oraciones negativas.

questions.question: We have ____ time to lose. (Nada de - verbo afirmativo).
questions.explanation: Have no time = no tener tiempo (no time to lose).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe el pronombre indefinido (someone, anything, nothing, etc.).

questions.question: I have ____ to tell you. (Algo)
Does ____ have a pen? (¿Alguien?)
There is ____ I can do. (Nada - verbo afirmativo)
I don't know ____. (Nada - verbo negativo)
____ is ready. (Todo)
____ left their laptop here. (Alguien)
I looked ____ for the file. (En todas partes)
I can't find it ____. (En ningún lado - verbo negativo)
____ wants to work on Sunday. (Nadie - verbo afirmativo)
____ agreed with the boss. (Todos)

pairs.target: En todas partes / En todos lados
